items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: So now I go to Murray. I says, 'well, the show's on. I can go back to New York.' He says, 'No, I want you to stay and conduct the show.' ... So now Murray Wanger wanted to -- it was so big that he had a place next door in a much more fabulous building he wanted to put this show in.

ctx.x: And so I started, made these arrangmeents. We had jungle numbers and all this. And so I told the guy, I said,

Murray, I said -- he just wanted to know how much it would be. I said, 'Well, you got to pay the guys so much, whatever the scale was, you got to pay them so much.' And for myself, I said, I'll go down. You know, he was short of money. So he said, 'What can you do?' I said, well, 'I'll put the band together, but the men will have to get paid. If you -- I'll go down and rehearse, you know, went to Miami a week ahead of time, and I'll write the music and rehearse the band, and when it is finished, you pay me for…

So anyway, we went -- I put this band together, three trumpets, one trombone, four saxes and rhythms, three rhythms, and we went to Miami, and I said, the guys have got to get a week's salary for the week that we're there rehearsing. Well, I sat down, and I didn't even go to rehearsal. I just sat and wrote the music and sent it out to rehearsal, and Cab rehearsed the band. And they put this show together.
